items.name: Crystal Lake Park
items.note: 25 acres of forested upland and wetland habitat (also salt marsh and a man-made pond); 0.5 mile loop trail, half boardwalk / half earthen around the lake; 124 Lady's Island Drive, Beaufort; dawn to dusk. County-managed.

items.name: Whitehall Park
items.note: 120 White Hall Drive, Lady's Island; 9.72 acres of mixed pine and live oak canopy along a salt marsh point on the Beaufort River; pavilion with restrooms and water fountains, picnic garden under live oak canopy, benches along the river front. (Search summary: county-owned, City of Beaufort maintains it.)

items.name: White Hall Boat Landing
items.note: County page states: access to Lady's Island-Factory Creek; four lane undivided ramp; limited parking (16 spaces); heavily used; older courtesy dock; drop-off at low tide. No address and no hours on the page.

items.name: Richard V. Woods Memorial Bridge
items.note: Swing bridge, opened 1959 as the Lady's Island Bridge, renamed 1971; added to the National Register of Historic Places January 2023 (search summary of Wikipedia/Explore Beaufort; Wikipedia page not opened).

items.name: Beaufort Executive Airport
items.note: County-owned public airport on Lady's Island (Wikipedia 'Beaufort County Airport' lead via search summary); renamed 2020; 39 Airport Circle, Beaufort SC 29907. Wikipedia Lady's Island article also states the Beaufort County Airport is on the island. It is a working airport, not a visitor attraction.

items.name: Whitehall Park / Crystal Lake Park
items.note: see things_to_do

items.name: Altamaha Town Heritage Preserve
items.note: County event page: '100-acre oak-hickory forested gem along the Okatie and Collecton [sic] Rivers'; off Old Bailey's Road near Okatie Highway (Hwy 170); listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994; 0.5 mile one-way earthen trail to a scenic view. (Trust for Public Land page returned 403; TPL summary via search only.)

items.name: Callawassie Island Sugar Works
items.note: Wikipedia: 'the only sugar mill ruins known to exist in South Carolina'; tabby ruins of a mill base and boiling house. It sits on gated Callawassie Island, so it is not publicly visitable: do not present it as a place to visit.

items.name: Old Barrel Landing School
items.note: SC Picture Project (not an official source): one-room school on SC Hwy 170, Okatie SC 29909; second school on the property; served grades 1-8 until a Bluffton consolidated school opened in 1919; later a community center; restored 1995. Search summary adds a 1995 historical marker (HMDB). No Rosenwald connection found. Treat as weak source.

items.name: Penn Center - York W. Bailey Museum
items.note: Penn Center visit page: museum Tuesday through Saturday 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.; docent-led tours at 10:00, 12:00, 3:00; 16 Penn Center Circle West, St. Helena Island SC 29920; 'Education for Freedom' exhibit on the 86-year history of the Penn School. Hours change; re-check before use.

items.name: Penn Center Heritage Days
items.note: Penn Center page: 'the annual Heritage Days Celebration each November'. Search summary: 41st edition was Nov 6-8 2025 (Explore Beaufort calendar); 2026 dates not found. Cite as annual event only.

items.name: Fort Fremont Preserve and History Center
items.note: County-owned, 1124 Land's End Road; dawn to dusk, free; fort built 1898; National Register. History center hours per April 2023 county notice (Fri 10-2, Sat 10-4, Sun 1-4): confirm current. Source summary says 18 acres on county pages vs 15 acres in a WTOC piece: do not quote acreage.

items.name: St. Helena Parish Chapel of Ease Ruins
items.note: NRHP ref 88001777, listed Oct 6 1988; junction of SC secondary roads 45 and 37 near Frogmore; built c. 1740; burned Feb 1886 (search summary of Wikipedia/NPS; NPS page not opened).

3.claim: Ridgeland incorporated 1894, Jasper County seat; Town runs its own planning/permits
3.verdict: verified (incorporation from the Town site; county seat from Wikipedia; own planning verified)
3.quote: Town of Ridgeland: 'Originally known as Gopher Hill, the Town of Ridgeland was incorporated in 1894.' 4.claim: Okatie spans Beaufort and Jasper counties; Callawassie Island ARC roof standards; Oldfield; Spring Island
4.verdict: Okatie: verified. Callawassie: verified (official POA document found). Oldfield: partly (no official source). Spring Island: not found.
4.quote: Wikipedia: Okatie is 'located in Beaufort and Jasper counties in the Lowcountry of South Carolina.' CALLAWASSIE ISLAND POA Design Standards and Guidelines (ARC), 'Updated December 12, 2023', Section III, 'Roof Materials and Accessories' (printed p.21-22): '(d) Roof materials may be asphalt or fiberglass shingles and must have a forty (40) year or approved "Lifetime" warranty.' '(e) Cedar shakes or shingles, slate and metal roofing are acceptable.' '(a) All roof accessories, such as vent pipes, including vent flashing, roof vents and roof fans, shall be painted to match the roof color.' '(c) Raw aluminum or galvanized flashing is not allowed. Flashing, except copper, must be painted to harmonize with the roof color.' Also 'All exposed metals (other than copper), including flashing, must be painted to match the adjacent material color.' and '(a) The roofs of all residences and accessory buildings shall have minimum pitch of 6/12.' Enforcement list: 'Any changes to the exterior of a home ... without ARC approval' is a violation. Oldfield: Okatie-page Wikipedia lists Oldfield; search summaries (golf/club sites, not official governing documents) call it an 860-acre private gated community on the Okatie River. Spring Island: no Spring Island Trust/ARB document found; earlier research noted its site says 'in Beaufort, SC' and Okatie is only a mailing address.
4.note: Nuance for copy: the standard names asphalt/fiberglass shingles with 40-year or approved Lifetime warranty (not 'any shingles'); minimum pitch 6/12. PDF text is encoded oddly - extracted with macOS PDFKit; the 'Building on Callawassie' page (https://www.callawassieisland.com/real-estate/building-on-callawassie/) links to it.

5.claim: Pritchardville: Bluffton drainage guidance (roofs and driveways add runoff; connect roofing to gutters/downspouts)
5.verdict: verified for runoff; DIFFERS on 'connect to gutters/downspouts'

The page does not tell homeowners to 'connect roofing to gutters' (only new single-family lots: Stormwater Design Manual disconnection of roof drains into vegetated areas - search summary).

bailey_bill.point: Invest at least 75% of the building's assessed value in eligible, approved work
bailey_bill.verdict: verified as the packet words it; differs slightly elsewhere
bailey_bill.quote: Packet p.1: 'If a property owner invests a minimum of 75% of their building's assessed value back into the building, and the work is eligible and approved...'. But the City FAQ says 'The minimum investment is 75% of the Fair Market Value of the building', and the Part A form asks for fair market value (FMV) of the building, determined by SC licensed appraisal within 45 days, bona fide sales contract within 12 months, or County Assessor. State law measures against fair market value, with the percentage set in the local ordinance (20%-100%).

bailey_bill.point: Assessed value frozen at the pre-rehabilitation value for 10 years
bailey_bill.quote: Packet p.1: 'the assessed value of the property is "frozen" at the pre-rehabilitation value for the next 10 years.' City FAQ repeats it. State law allows up to 20 years; the length is set by local ordinance ('not more than twenty years', SC Code 4-9-195(B)(4)). The City/County ordinance text itself was not found.

bailey_bill.point: Eligible: Historic District and at least 50 years old, or on the 1997 Beaufort County Above Ground Historic Sites Survey
bailey_bill.quote: Packet: 'Be located in the Historic District and be at least 50 years old; or Be listed on the 1997 Beaufort County Above Ground Historic Sites Survey.' Part A form also offers 'Contributing structure in the Historic District', 'Non-contributing structure, but over 50 years old, and in the Historic District', or 'outside of the Historic District, but listed on the Beaufort County 1997 Historic Survey'.

bailey_bill.point: Roof listed as an element on the Part A form
bailey_bill.quote: Part A, section 5: 'Architectural elements would include items such as: roof; exterior brick or siding; porches; exterior elevations; windows; doors...'. The packet's worked example also counts 'a new roof' toward the 75%.

bailey_bill.point: Process: pre-application conference, HRB project application, agreement, final review
bailey_bill.quote: '1. Potential applicants must attend the Pre-Application Conference.' '2. Applicant must fill out an Historic Review Board (HRB) Project Application, as well as a Part A - Bailey Bill Preliminary Review Application.' '3. If a project is approved, the owner must sign a Memorandum of Understanding...' '4. When the project is completed, the applicant files a Part B - Bailey Bill Final Review Application with city staff.' Also: fee $150 (single-family/duplex) / $300 (other); owner applies separately to the Beaufort County Auditor (auditor form, search summary).
'6. If the property is sold within the 10 year period, the balance of the tax freeze period transfers to the new owner.'

bailey_bill.verdict: differs in citation: 4-9-195 is the COUNTY enabling statute; municipalities get it through 5-21-140; the packet itself cites Title 12 (12-120 to 12-125) for definitions
bailey_bill.quote: SC Code 5-21-140: 'The powers and authorities conferred upon county governing bodies by Section 4-9-195 are also conferred' on municipal governing bodies. 4-9-195: county may grant the special assessment by ordinance; historic property listed in the National Register or at least fifty years old and designated; minimum rehabilitation expenditures 'between twenty percent and one hundred percent' of fair market value; period 'of not more than twenty years'. The packet cites 'South Carolina 1976 Code Sections 12-120 through 12-125' and 'SC 12-120.D'.

bailey_bill.point: Is the packet still the current one?
bailey_bill.verdict: no newer version found; not proven current
bailey_bill.quote: Packet footer 'Revised 3/18/2019'. The City's current FAQ page (cityofbeaufort.org/m/faq?cat=28) states the same 75%/10-year/eligibility terms and lists the same forms (Part A, Memorandum of Understanding, Part B). A Beaufort County Auditor Bailey Bill form dated 08/2023 exists (not opened). No newer City packet or ordinance found; the ordinance text was not found. Packet's own web link (cityofbeaufort.org/bailey-bill.aspx) is the old site.

st_helena_cpo.what_it_says: A Purpose; B District Boundaries ('shown on the Beaufort County Official Zoning Map... the permitted uses shall be limited to the base zoning, except where additional limitations are established within the CPO zone'); C Site Design ('Design features that restrict access to water and other culturally significant locations, and franchise design are prohibited'); D Use Limitations (prohibits gated communities, golf courses, resorts and similar large-scale development).
st_helena_cpo.roofs_or_exterior: NOT FOUND. No wording on roofs, roofing materials or exterior changes in the 3.4.50 text read. Only 'franchise design' under Site Design touches building appearance.

new_riverside_permit_authority.what_was_found: No official page states who issues building permits for the New Riverside communities. Town of Bluffton applications page lists a re-roof form but says nothing about which areas its permits cover and does not mention New Riverside. Beaufort County Building Codes requirements page does not mention roofing or New Riverside; contact (843) 255-2078. A search summary (non-official) says the Town approved the New Riverside Concept Plan and Development Agreement in June 2004 and Bluffton Planning Commission reviews New Riverside parcels (e.g. Parcel 8A, April 2026), which suggests Town jurisdiction, but this is NOT an official statement of permit authority.
